title: AWS Certified Example Title
description: Breve descrição sobre o propósito desta certificação.

questions.statement: A company is looking for a storage solution for static web assets that provides low latency globally. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Host assets on Amazon S3 and distribute them globally via Amazon CloudFront.
options.explanation: Correct: S3 combined with CloudFront edge locations provides high durability and low-latency global delivery.

options.text: Store assets on Amazon EBS volumes attached to a single EC2 instance.
options.explanation: Incorrect: EBS is block storage tied to a single AZ and does not scale globally.

options.text: Store files on AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway.
options.explanation: Incorrect: Storage Gateway is designed for hybrid on-premises environments, not low latency web asset distribution.

options.text: Use Amazon DynamoDB to store large image files as binary attributes.
options.explanation: Incorrect: DynamoDB item limit is 400KB and is not meant for direct public static web asset hosting.

questions.generalExplanation: Amazon CloudFront in front of an Amazon S3 bucket is the AWS best practice for secure and low-latency global static asset delivery.

questions.statement: A financial firm requires that all data stored at rest in Amazon S3 must be encrypted using customer-managed keys that are automatically rotated annually. Which TWO steps should the solutions architect take? (Choose TWO.)

options.text: Create an AWS KMS customer managed key (CMK) and enable automatic key rotation.
options.explanation: Correct: AWS KMS customer managed keys support automatic annual rotation.

options.text: Configure the S3 bucket default encryption to use SSE-KMS with the created customer managed key.
options.explanation: Correct: Default bucket encryption ensures all new objects are encrypted with the specified CMK.

options.text: Use AWS KMS AWS managed key (aws/s3).
options.explanation: Incorrect: AWS managed keys cannot be customized or manually managed, and rotate every 3 years.

options.text: Enable SSE-S3 encryption on the S3 bucket.
options.explanation: Incorrect: SSE-S3 uses 256-bit AES keys managed by S3, not customer managed KMS keys.

options.text: Create an asymmetric KMS key pair and store the private key in AWS Secrets Manager.
options.explanation: Incorrect: S3 server-side encryption requires symmetric KMS keys.

questions.generalExplanation: To satisfy customer-managed key requirements with annual rotation, create a symmetric KMS CMK with key rotation enabled and configure S3 bucket default encryption with SSE-KMS.
